questions.problem:
In a garden, $60%$ of the flowers are roses. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that if $100$ flowers are picked at random, then $70$ of them will be roses. Give your answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ | $\,0.9732\,$ | $\,0.9738\,$ |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ | $\,0.9788\,$ | $\,0.9793\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ | $\,0.9834\,$ | $\,0.9838\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=100$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =100\cdot 0.6 \\  & =60 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =100\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =40 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(100)(0.6)=60
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(100)(0.6)(1-0.6)=24.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(60,24).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=70).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=70)≈P(69.5\le Y\le 70.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(69.5\le Y\le 70.5) & =P(\frac{69.5-60}{\sqrt{24}}\le Z\le \frac{70.5-60}{\sqrt{24}}) \\  & ≈P(1.94\le Z\le 2.14) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.14)-P(Z<1.94) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.14)-P(Z\le 1.94) \\  & =Φ(2.14)-Φ(1.94) \\  & =0.9838-0.9738 \\  & =0.010\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=70)≈0.010.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0102.$

questions.problem:
In a music program at a college, an average of $45%$ of graduating students go on to pursue a career in music. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, estimate the probability that in a graduating class of $200$ students, at least $110$ students will go on to pursue a career in music. Give your final answer to $3$ decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.6\,$ | $\,0.9960\,$ | $\,0.9961\,$ | $\,0.9962\,$ |
| $\,2.7\,$ | $\,0.9970\,$ | $\,0.9971\,$ | $\,0.9972\,$ |
| $\,2.8\,$ | $\,0.9978\,$ | $\,0.9979\,$ | $\,0.9979\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=200$ and $p=0.45.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =200\cdot 0.45 \\  & =90 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =200\cdot (1-0.45) \\  & =110 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(200)(0.45)=90
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(200)(0.45)(1-0.45)=49.5.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(90,49.5).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(X\ge 110).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X\ge 110)≈P(Y>109.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>109.5) & =1-P(Y\le 109.5) \\  & =1-P(Z\le \frac{109.5-90}{\sqrt{49.5}}) \\  & ≈1-P(Z\le 2.77) \\  & =1-Φ(2.77) \\  & =1-0.9972 \\  & =0.0028\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X\ge 110)≈0.003.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0028.$

questions.problem:
Which of the following probabilities could be approximated using the normal approximation of the binomial distribution?

I. The probability that $5$ flights out of $50$ arrive late at an airport if the probability of arriving late is $0.09$ for each flight.

II. The probability that a student correctly solves $3$ questions in a $5$-question math test if the student has a $46%$ probability of correctly answering each question.

III. The probability that a biased coin lands on heads more than $30$ times out of $80$ coin flips if the probability of a single flip landing on heads is $0.52.$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Let's now examine each situation.

- In situation I, we have $n=50$ and $p=0.09.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =50\cdot 0.09 \\  & =4.5 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation II, we have $n=5$ and $p=0.46.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =5\cdot 0.46 \\  & =2.3 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation III, we have $n=80$ and $p=0.52.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =80\cdot 0.52 \\  & =41.6 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =80\cdot (1-0.52) \\  & =38.4 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

questions.problem:
Which of the following probabilities could be approximated using the normal approximation of the binomial distribution?

I. The probability of getting $48$ even numbers on $100$ rolls of a $6$-sided die.

II. The probability that less than $4$ wireless earphones are defective from a box containing $30$ pairs of earphones if the probability of a single pair being defective is $0.15.$

III. The probability that a basketball player scores $8$ of $20$ three-point shots if the probability of scoring each shot is $0.53.$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Let's now examine each situation.

- In situation I, we have $n=100$ and $p=\frac{1}{6}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =100\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{50}{3} \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =100\cdot (1-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{250}{3} \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation II, we have $n=30$ and $p=0.15.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =30\cdot 0.15 \\  & =4.5 \\  & ≯5.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, we *cannot* use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

- In situation III, we have $n=20$ and $p=0.53.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =20\cdot 0.53 \\  & =10.6 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =20\cdot (1-0.53) \\  & =9.4 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can use the normal approximation of the binomial distribution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=165$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =165\cdot 0.6 \\  & =99 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =165\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =66 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(165)(0.6)=99
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(165)(0.6)(1-0.6)=39.6.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(99,39.6).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=90).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=90)≈P(89.5\le Y\le 90.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(89.5\le Y\le 90.5) & =P(\frac{89.5-99}{\sqrt{39.6}}\le Z\le \frac{90.5-99}{\sqrt{39.6}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.51\le Z\le -1.35) \\  & =P(Z\le -1.35)-P(Z<-1.51) \\  & =P(Z\le -1.35)-P(Z\le -1.51) \\  & =Φ(-1.35)-Φ(-1.51) \\  & =0.0885-0.0655 \\  & =0.023\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=90)≈0.023.
$$
